title: European Parliament to open Ottawa office as Carney seeks 'unique alliance' with EU

image.caption: Prime Minister Mark Carney meets with the President of the European Parliament Roberta Metsola in Yerevan, Armenia, on May 3, 2026. Carney will address the European Parliament on Thursday. (Sean Kilpatrick/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: The European Parliament, a key institution of the European Union, is set to open an "antenna" office in Canada's national capital as Prime Minister Mark Carney looks to deepen ties with the 27-member bloc.
Carney set to address the elected body on Thursday

"Europe and Canada share values, interests and a commitment to the same rules-based international order. Our new presence in Ottawa will turn that partnership into even closer parliamentary co-operation," Roberta Metsola, president of the European Parliament, said in a news release on Monday.
Ottawa would be the 10th city where such an office is located, according to the news release, and the third in North America after New York and Washington.

The parliament is a representative body of elected members from the states that make up the EU. The EU already has an embassy in Ottawa, but it's run by the European Commission which is the executive branch of the bloc and separate from the parliament.

items: Carney says Canada planning to discuss 'unique alliance' with EU, but not membership

blocks.text: Carney said on Sunday that his government plans to begin discussions for a "unique alliance" with the European Union — but not membership — as he gears up to address the European Parliament this week.

"What we are looking — and will begin discussions for — [is] a unique alliance with the European Union. We share the same values, we have the same priorities and we have very complementary strengths," he said.

Darren Major is a senior writer for CBC's parliamentary bureau in Ottawa. He previously worked as a digital reporter for CBC Ottawa and a producer for CBC's Power & Politics. He holds a master's degree in journalism and a bachelor's degree in public affairs and policy management, both from Carleton University. He also holds a master's degree in arts from Queen's University. He can be reached at darren.major@cbc.ca.
